A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoSE work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training, downstream evaluation, inference-mode comparisons, and routing and width analyses in Section 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds larger-model evaluations, continual-pretraining experiments, reasoning benchmarks, and runtime and routing diagnostics.

M1.justification: v2 adds a continual-pretraining pathway that initializes from an existing non-slimmable MoE checkpoint and continues training under the MoSE objective (Section 2.3 and Appendix D). This extends the training workflow; the nested expert architecture, two-width objective, and inference allocation rules remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated zero-shot tasks on HellaSwag, PIQA, and Social IQA, extending coverage to multiple-choice completion, physical commonsense, and social commonsense reasoning (Table 2 and Appendix A.1). The original OpenWebText, WikiText-103, LAMBADA, and WSC coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain vanilla MoE and the same uniform-width, normalized-probability, shared-gamma, and layer-wise-gamma comparisons. Added scale and task evaluations reuse these approaches. DeepSeek supplies a pretrained backbone; RoE and EMoE remain related-work citations rather than newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New settings include GPT2-Large with 2.5B parameters and 50B training tokens, E64A8/E128A8 routing, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite adaptation. Appendix D introduces 0.5%/5% continued-training comparisons, while Appendices B.4–B.5 add runtime and routing-distribution measurement protocols. The original experiments' stated settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of whether FLOPs predict measured latency/throughput and whether width sampling preserves routing balance and expert-selection distributions (Figures 16–19). Figures 21–22 analyze adaptation budget and width-specific recovery during continual pretraining. Original ablations and routing-transfer analyses remain, including the E8A4 study relocated to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Figure 16 introduces fitted linear runtime-versus-FLOPs relationships, reporting coefficients and R-squared values. This adds statistical estimation, but neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New evaluations report 32.8% and 38.1% matched-perplexity FLOP reductions for GPT2-Large and adapted DeepSeek-V2-Lite, respectively (Figures 10 and 12). Table 2 adds reasoning scores, including HellaSwag accuracy of 0.335 for MoE versus 0.385 for MoSE. CPT and diagnostic findings are also added. The original Table 1 values and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 corrects the description of the selected-expert set S(x): v1 specifies zero routing weights, whereas v2 correctly specifies nonzero weights, resolving the inconsistency with Equation 7. The numbered equations otherwise remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement broaden the demonstrated applicability from scratch-trained GPT models to pretrained modern MoEs adapted through continual pretraining, alongside additional reasoning tasks. Posttraining slimmability, explicitly left open in v1, becomes a demonstrated capability. The conclusion also replaces latency-scaling wording with a compute-quality claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets continual pretraining as a practical adaptation route while explaining its trade-off against stronger full-pretraining frontiers. The remaining scale limitation becomes frontier-scale training from scratch. New discussion qualifies FLOPs-to-runtime generalization on memory-bound hardware, interprets routing stability across widths, and identifies width-dependent safety evaluation as a consideration.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access URL, architectural and training-schedule details for the additional configurations in Table 3, Blackwell GPU information, and CPT initialization/corpus information. Existing optimizer, width-grid, calibration-budget, and gamma-optimization details remain unchanged; the additions supplement the original reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the new reasoning benchmarks, DeepSeek-V3, Llama, and Medusa, and removes the adaptive-complexity hyperparameter-transfer reference. Positioning relative to slimmable networks, RoE, and EMoE remains essentially unchanged. DeepSeek-V2 authorship and the agent-paper publication updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.4, reorganizes supplementary material into Appendices B–D, moves the E8A4 discussion to Appendix C, and reorders the ablation and transfer discussions. It locally revises explanations, the abstract, limitations, impact statement, and conclusion, while retaining most original prose and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds nine figures covering scale, adaptation, runtime, and routing diagnostics, adds the reasoning-results table, and expands the architecture table. All thirteen original graphics are retained with placement and numbering changes; notably, v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 20.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's explicit open question about acquiring slimmability after pretraining through CPT and DeepSeek experiments. Measured runtime validation, routing diagnostics, and broader task and scale evaluations substantially strengthen the evidence for practical applicability while preserving the original results. CPT/runtime protocols remain incompletely specified and run-to-run uncertainty is absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the important empirical gaps addressed.
